prompt_text:
<TASK_CONTRACT>
BOUNDARY_CONTRACT_VERSION: chapter3-boundary-sync-v1
TASK_STAGE: entity-only

Extract only these four entity types:
- Vulnerability: every explicit CVE identifier mention. Preserve PDF spacing or hyphen breaks in text and normalize the identifier.
- Weakness: an explicit CWE identifier, or a descriptive flaw phrase uniquely tied to an explicit CWE in the same local fact block. A description-only phrase without a locally explicit CWE is out of scope. Never infer a CWE from model knowledge or an external CVE-CWE mapping.
- Configuration: the shortest independently identifiable concrete product, component, device, or complete CPE mention that can serve as the tail of a directly supported Vulnerability-affects->Configuration fact. Exclude ordinary versions, patches, builds, incidental vendors, tools, services, filenames, IP addresses, ports, and generic product placeholders.
- AttackTechnique: an explicit ATT&CK T-code or a technique name that is uniquely normalizable from the local text. When a name and its T-code are adjacent, retain only the T-code. TA tactic IDs and S/G/C identifiers are out of scope.

Entity rules:
1. Entity text must be an exact substring of the input.
2. start/end are 0-based offsets and end is exclusive; text[start:end] must equal entity text.
3. Extract every distinct explicit mention; do not duplicate the same type and span.
4. normalized_id uses the canonical CVE, locally explicit CWE, verified CPE 2.3 URI, or ATT&CK T-code; otherwise null.
5. Output entities only. Stage 1 must not extract, define, or output relations.
6. Return exactly these entity fields: id, text, type, start, end, normalized_id.

Frozen reference examples:
<example>
<text>
Attackers exploited CVE-2021-44228 in the Log4j component to gain initial access by exploiting a public-facing application (T1190).
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2021-44228", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 20, "end": 34, "normalized_id": "CVE-2021-44228"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "Log4j", "type": "Configuration", "start": 42, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:apache:log4j:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "T1190", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 124, "end": 129, "normalized_id": "T1190"}
]
</entities>
</example>

<example>
<text>
CVE-2021-26855 is a server-side request forgery (CWE-918) vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server.
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2021-26855", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 14, "normalized_id": "CVE-2021-26855"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "server-side request forgery", "type": "Weakness", "start": 20, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "CWE-918"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "CWE-918", "type": "Weakness", "start": 49, "end": 56, "normalized_id": "CWE-918"},
  {"id": "E4", "text": "Microsoft Exchange Server", "type": "Configuration", "start": 75, "end": 100, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:microsoft:exchange_server:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"}
]
</entities>
</example>

Input text:
<text>
{text}
</text>

Return one JSON object only:
{"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "exact substring", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 14, "normalized_id": "CVE-..."}]}
</TASK_CONTRACT>

<OPERATIONAL_GUIDANCE>
Scan the entire input, including prose, tables, lists, captions, and line-broken identifiers. Apply the frozen definitions conservatively and check every emitted span against the source before returning JSON.

CONFIGURATION ELIGIBILITY AND SPAN TESTS - apply in order for every candidate:

1. Canonical product-only eligibility: Emit a Configuration only if the substring itself names a concrete vendor product, component, device model, or complete CPE string that is independently identifiable without surrounding context. If the phrase needs surrounding vulnerability context to seem like a product, skip it.

2. Strip to base form and adjust offsets: The emitted span must exclude instance numerals, deployment qualifiers, plural inflection, and version-like suffixes. Adjust start/end to cover only the base product substring so text[start:end] equals the emitted text.
- Instance numerals: "ExampleApp 1", "ExampleApp 2" -> emit "ExampleApp" for each occurrence, with span covering only "ExampleApp", never including " 1" / " 2".
- Deployment / status qualifiers: "public-facing ExampleApp", "affected ExampleApp", "compromised ExampleApp" -> emit only "ExampleApp".
- Plural inflection: if source writes pluralized product such as "ExampleApps", emit only the singular base "ExampleApp" with end offset reduced by 1 to exclude trailing "s". If no singular base is present as substring, skip.
- Versions, patches, builds: never include them in span.

3. Explicit forbiddens even adjacent to vulnerability context: Never emit generic infrastructure-role nouns, incidental actor/defender tools, files, or deployment-specific labels, even when sentence says vulnerability was exploited on/in them or they were used for scanning, proxying, archiving, or persistence.
- Forbid: "Web Server", "endpoint", "workstation", "network", "agency", "server" alone, "EDR tool", "scanner", "proxy tool", "archive tool", "trojan multi-tool", filenames, script names (.exe, .rar, .zip, .sh, .jsp, .ashx), IP addresses, ports, service names, vendor alone, generic placeholders.
- Contrast: In "exploited flaw in Acme Portal on public-facing host using ScannerTool", POSITIVE is "Acme Portal" only. NEGATIVE - do not emit "public-facing host", "host", or "ScannerTool".

4. Multi-token suite vs base product:
- Keep whole only when the contiguous phrase is the official product-family name as written (vendor + product + edition family). Example POSITIVE: "Acme Portal Data Center and Server" kept as one span when that full family phrase appears contiguously, minus any instance numeral.
- Reduce when second part is deployment/instance context, not part of family name. Example: "Acme Portal on Web Server" -> emit only "Acme Portal", never "Acme Portal on Web Server" and never "Web Server".
- Never create a suite span by joining non-contiguous tokens or by adding qualifiers from elsewhere in the sentence.

5. normalized_id constraint: Set normalized_id only to a verified base-product CPE 2.3 URI for vendor:product. Never construct a CPE by concatenating edition words, suite connectors, numerals, or qualifiers with underscores. If no confident verified base-product mapping exists, use null.
- POSITIVE: "Acme Portal" -> "cpe:2.3:a:acme:portal:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*" if verified, else null.
- NEGATIVE: do not emit "cpe:2.3:a:acme:portal_data_center_and_server:..." by joining span tokens, and do not invent a product token from an instance label or plural form.

If any test fails, skip the candidate. When in doubt between emitting a longer qualified span versus a shorter base span, emit the shorter base span. When in doubt between emitting a generic noun versus nothing, emit nothing.
</OPERATIONAL_GUIDANCE>

Follow the immutable contract and the operational guidance. Output JSON only.

prompt_text:
You are an entity extractor for cybersecurity reports. Perform entity-only extraction. Do not extract relations.

GOAL
Read the supplied passage and list every explicit mention of the four allowed categories below. Do not create any other label and do not output relationships.

ALLOWED CATEGORIES

1. Vulnerability — Any directly written CVE ID. Keep the surface form exactly as it appears, including odd spacing or line-break hyphens from PDFs, but put the cleaned canonical form in normalized_id.

2. Weakness — Either:
   a) a directly written CWE ID, or
   b) a natural-language flaw description that is explicitly linked to a CWE ID inside the same nearby factual unit.
   If there is no CWE ID written nearby in the text, do not tag a generic flaw description. Never guess a CWE from background knowledge or from a known CVE-to-CWE mapping.

3. Configuration — The minimal standalone name of a specific vendor product, software component, hardware device, or a full CPE string that could plausibly be the target of a Vulnerability-affects-Configuration statement.
   Keep only independently recognizable products. Omit version numbers, patch/build strings, vendor names alone, attacker or defender utilities, scanners, proxies, services, file/script names, IP addresses, ports, and vague placeholders like “server” or “endpoint”.

4. AttackTechnique — A directly written MITRE ATT&CK technique code (Txxxx) or a technique name that can be mapped to a single T-code purely from the wording in the passage. If a name appears immediately next to its code, keep the code only and drop the name. Do not tag tactic IDs starting with TA, nor software/group/campaign IDs starting with S/G/C.

CORE SPAN AND OUTPUT RULES
- Every `text` must occur verbatim in the input. `start` is inclusive, `end` is exclusive, both 0-based, and `text` must equal input[start:end].
- Tag each distinct occurrence separately; never emit two items with identical type and identical span.
- `normalized_id` must be: canonical CVE for Vulnerability, the locally written CWE for Weakness, a verified CPE 2.3 URI for Configuration, or the T-code for AttackTechnique. Use null when no verified value applies.
- Emit entities only. Do not define, infer, or print relations.
- Check the whole document: body paragraphs, tables, bullet lists, figure captions, and identifiers split across lines.

PRODUCT MENTION FILTER — evaluate every Configuration candidate in this order, skip if it fails:

A. Standalone recognizability: The substring alone must identify a concrete product/component/device/CPE without needing the surrounding vulnerability sentence. If it only looks like a product because of context, discard it.

B. Reduce to base name and fix offsets:
- Remove instance numbers: for “MyApp 1” / “MyApp 2” keep only “MyApp” with offsets covering just that word.
- Remove deployment adjectives: for “affected MyApp”, “public-facing MyApp”, “compromised MyApp” keep only “MyApp”.
- De-pluralize: if written as “MyApps”, keep only “MyApp” and shorten `end` by 1 to drop the trailing “s”. If no singular substring exists, discard.
- Never include version, patch, or build tokens in the span.

C. Hard exclusions even near exploit language: Never tag role nouns, generic infrastructure, security tooling, or operational artifacts, even if the sentence says the flaw was exploited on them or they were used for scanning, proxying, archiving, or persistence.
Examples to reject: Web Server, host, endpoint, workstation, network, agency, server alone, EDR, scanner, proxy, archiver, multi-tool, .exe/.rar/.zip/.sh/.jsp/.ashx names, IPs, ports, service labels, lone vendor, generic placeholders.
Illustration: in “flaw in Acme Portal on public-facing host using ScannerTool” the only valid product is “Acme Portal”.

D. Suite versus base:
- Keep a long multi-word span only when that contiguous string is the official family/edition name as printed, e.g. “Acme Portal Data Center and Server” when it appears contiguously as a family label, minus any instance number.
- Shorten when the extra words are location/deployment context, e.g. “Acme Portal on Web Server” -> keep only “Acme Portal”.
- Never assemble a span from non-adjacent tokens or import qualifiers from elsewhere.

E. Normalization for products: `normalized_id` may only be a verified base vendor:product CPE 2.3 URI. Do not build a CPE by joining edition words or numbers with underscores and do not invent tokens from instance labels or plurals. Example: “Acme Portal” may map to “cpe:2.3:a:acme:portal:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*” if verified, otherwise null. If uncertain, use null.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLES — follow the same logic, do not copy spans:

Example 1
Input: CVE-2023-1234 in MyApp exploited via T1059.
Output:
{"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2023-1234", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 13, "normalized_id": "CVE-2023-1234"}, {"id": "E2", "text": "MyApp", "type": "Configuration", "start": 17, "end": 22, "normalized_id": null}, {"id": "E3", "text": "T1059", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 37, "end": 42, "normalized_id": "T1059"}]}

Example 2
Input: Buffer overflow (CWE-119) in FooBar from CVE-2024-0001.
Output:
{"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "Buffer overflow", "type": "Weakness", "start": 0, "end": 15, "normalized_id": "CWE-119"}, {"id": "E2", "text": "CWE-119", "type": "Weakness", "start": 17, "end": 24, "normalized_id": "CWE-119"}, {"id": "E3", "text": "FooBar", "type": "Configuration", "start": 29, "end": 35, "normalized_id": null}, {"id": "E4", "text": "CVE-2024-0001", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 41, "end": 54, "normalized_id": "CVE-2024-0001"}]}

DOCUMENT TO PROCESS
<text>
{text}
</text>

RESPONSE FORMAT
Return a single JSON object and nothing else, with this shape:
{"entities": [{"id": "E1", "text": "exact substring", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 13, "normalized_id": "CVE-..."}]}
Each item must contain exactly these fields: "id", "text", "type", "start", "end", "normalized_id". If no entities are found, return {"entities": []}.

prompt_text:
PHASE: Standalone Entities Only — Cyber Threat Knowledge Harvest

Goal: Identify and mark up every in-scope entity mention appearing on its own. Do not wait for a second entity type to appear nearby — tag each mention independently.

Tag these four categories and nothing else:

• Vulnerability — Any literal CVE code written as CVE-YYYY-NNNN (or with extra digits). Keep the surface form exactly as printed, but set the normalized form to the standard uppercase CVE representation.

• Weakness — Either a literal CWE code such as CWE-XXX, or a natural-language flaw description that is explicitly linked to a CWE code inside the same immediate factual context. A generic flaw description with no CWE code visible in that local block must be ignored. Do not guess a CWE from background knowledge and do not use an external CVE-to-CWE lookup.

• Configuration — Only the in-scope system under analysis that can be vulnerable or targeted: an installed operating system, application, firmware / OS distribution, or hardware device / appliance.
  Positive scope: a specific real product, platform, OS, hardware device, or software component that is installed, runs, or is attacked, plus any full CPE string if shown. A Configuration mention is valid by itself; it does not need to be tied to a future link. Tag it everywhere it occurs — titles, headers, body paragraphs, tables, bulleted lists, figure captions, footnotes — not just next to a Vulnerability.
  Explicit deny — never tag:
  a. dual-use command-line utilities and data-transfer / sync tools used by actors;
  b. attacker proxy / transfer / scan / discovery tooling and post-exploitation frameworks;
  c. defender scanner / assessment products and services;
  d. cloud / hosting / service providers and generic infrastructure operators;
  e. generic application families, general tools, services, pure feature phrases;
  f. file names, commands / flags, scripts, IP addresses, port numbers, URLs;
  g. bare versions / patches / builds / updates, or vague placeholders.
  If the surface form is functioning as the technique label immediately adjacent to its technique code — e.g., Name (TXXXX) — tag only the T-code as AttackTechnique and suppress any Configuration tag on the name, even if the name resembles a utility or platform.
  How to choose the span — shortest self-identifying core, deterministically:
  a. Begin with the full noun phrase and shrink to the minimal token(s) that still independently identify the product.
  b. Mandatory strip of leading vendor / maker token when the product alone is distinctive and self-identifying; keep vendor+product together only if the product word alone is too generic and the vendor pairing is required to recognize it.
  c. Mandatory strip of trailing release information — version numbers, patches, builds, updates, and similar qualifiers. A version string by itself is never a valid span and a version token can never be part of the span.
  d. No merging of product + feature / function / module / sub-component chain. Keep only the head product. Do not combine a product with a following capability chain into one long mention.
  e. Do not tag stand-alone incidental vendors, utilities, services, file names, IPs, ports, plain versions / patches / builds, or generic product placeholders.

• AttackTechnique — Either a literal ATT&CK technique code like TXXXX (including dotted sub-techniques) or a technique name that can be unambiguously mapped from the surrounding wording. If a name sits directly next to its T-code, keep only the T-code mention. Tactic TA-IDs and software / group / campaign S/G/C IDs are excluded.

Strict handling rules:
1. The `text` of every entity must occur verbatim in the source.
2. `start` and `end` are zero-based character offsets with exclusive `end`, so that slicing the source as source[start:end] reproduces `text` exactly.
3. Capture each separate occurrence at its own location, including repetitions across headings, prose, tables and lists. Never collapse duplicates from different spans, never omit title/header occurrences, and never emit the same type over the identical span twice.
4. `normalized_id` must be the canonical CVE, the locally-shown CWE, an attested CPE 2.3 URI, or the ATT&CK T-code; use null otherwise. For Configuration, only use a confirmed canonical CPE 2.3 URI — if the part/vendor/product is doubtful, use null. Do not fabricate a CPE by lower-casing, concatenating, or adding underscores to display words.
5. Emit entities alone. Do not extract, invent, or print relationships.
6. Every entity object must contain exactly these members: `id`, `text`, `type`, `start`, `end`, `normalized_id`, and the top-level object must have the single key `entities`.

<text>
Attackers exploited CVE-2021-44228 in the Log4j component to gain initial access by exploiting a public-facing application (T1190).
</text>

]

  {"id": "E2", "text": "server-side request forgery", "type": "Weakness", "start": 20, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "CWE-918"},
